title: Dispatch: Lifecycle-graph closure pass over campaign-rule domain and store (PR #524 review 7, head 4aaf5e8)
description:
LIFECYCLE-GRAPH CLOSURE PASS over eshyra-jhpt.1/.2 at PR #524 head 4aaf5e8, triggered by external review #5119845911 (2026-09-05) and the reviewer's process note: four consecutive single-blocker rounds all sat in the same lifecycle/state-integrity family, so this round must exhaust the family rather than fix one edge. The supervisor enumerated the state machine (statuses active/superseded/revoked; transitions create/supersede/revoke; temporal relations before/equal/after current, predecessor, successor, revocation; chains A->B, A->B->C, later revoke, scheduled successor, cancellation before effect; disputed-turn vs prospective; validator vs store; read/list/active-at-position; checkpoint; rejected-mutation atomicity) and PROBED every suspect cell at 4aaf5e8. Five cells are defective. Fix ALL of them in this one dispatch.

WORKTREE / BRANCH: .worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev15 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev15, cut from eshyra-jhpt at 4aaf5e8. npm ci already run.

# =============================================================
F1 (BLOCKING, reviewer) — validateCampaignRules accepts reverse-time supersession.
Probe: validateCampaignRules([A effective P10 superseded-by B, B effective P5]) -> OK. The store rejects the same transition ("successor 'B' cannot take effect before 'A'"). activeRows would end A at B.effective (P5) so A is never active.
FIX: in the relation loop, fail when compareCampaignPositions(successor.effectivePosition, rule.effectivePosition) < 0 with the message `successor '${successor}' cannot take effect before '${rule}'` (same wording as the store). Equal positions remain accepted (the store accepts them; a scheduled prior replaced by a same-position successor is coherent — probe D2 confirmed prior never active, successor active).

# =============================================================
F2 (BLOCKING, supervisor) — cancelling a scheduled successor strands its prior.
Probe at 4aaf5e8: A effective 1 (active); after ten committed turns, supersede A with B effective 15 (scheduled); revoke B at 11 (cancellation, allowed since rev10 E5). Result: active set at 12 = [A], at 15 = [], at 20 = []; revokeCampaignRule(A) -> "campaign rule 'A' is not active"; supersedeCampaignRule(A) -> "campaign rule 'A' is already superseded"; validateCampaignRules(listCampaignRules) -> accepts. So A silently dies at 15 although its replacement never took effect, and A can never again be revoked or superseded. Both the store (producer) and the validator (acceptor) are wrong.
FIX (supervisor decision): forbid cancelling a successor before it takes effect. In revokeCampaignRule, after loading `existing`, look up whether any rule in the campaign has supersededBy === existing.ruleIdentity (single query); if so AND the canonical revokedPosition compares <= existing.effectivePosition, reject with `campaign rule '${B}' supersedes '${A}' and cannot be revoked before it takes effect; supersede it instead`. Revoking a successor AT OR AFTER its effective position stays allowed (A ends at B.effective, B active until revoked). Cancellation of a scheduled rule that supersedes nothing stays allowed (rev10 E5). Mirror in validateCampaignRules: for every superseded rule whose successor has revokedPosition !== null and compareCampaignPositions(successor.revokedPosition, successor.effectivePosition) <= 0, fail with `successor '${B}' of '${A}' was revoked before taking effect`. Document in the module comment that "cancelling a scheduled replacement" is expressed as superseding the scheduled successor with a new rule (typically a copy of the prior's prose) effective at the same position, which keeps continuity: prior until P, replacement from P.

# =============================================================
F3 (supervisor) — validateCampaignRules accepts two priors naming the same successor.
Probe: [A1 superseded-by B, A2 superseded-by B, B] -> OK. The store cannot produce this (a successor is written once through supersede and must not already exist), so the validator certifies structurally impossible history. FIX: fail `campaign rule '${B}' is named as successor by more than one rule` when a successor identity is referenced by two or more supersededBy values.

# =============================================================
F4 (supervisor) — validateCampaignRules accepts overlapping active rulings for one ambiguity.
Probe: two ambiguity rulings for 'amb', R1 effective 1 and R2 effective 2, both active -> OK. The store rejects this at write time (assertNoOverlappingAmbiguityRuling) and the context assembler fails closed on conflicting active rulings, so the validator accepts history the runtime treats as unplayable. FIX: add a set-level overlap check mirroring the store's half-open interval algebra: interval start = effectivePosition; end = revokedPosition for revoked rules, successor.effectivePosition (resolved via the same byId map) for superseded rules, open for active rules; intervals with end <= start are empty and never overlap; two rulings with the same provenance.ambiguityId whose intervals overlap fail with `active ambiguity ruling '${x}' overlaps '${y}' for ambiguity '${id}'` (store wording). Factor the interval algebra into ONE exported helper in campaignRules.ts and make the store's intervalsOverlap/existingIntervalEnd use it (behaviour identical; keep the store's pending-successor case).

# =============================================================
F5 (low, supervisor) — hydration symmetry. rowToRule fails closed on status/revoked_position mismatch (rev11) but not on status/superseded_by mismatch; the SQLite CHECK constraint covers the latter today, but a materialized snapshot from a future schema, or any other row source, would hydrate a superseded row without a successor as if coherent. FIX: in rowToRule, fail `superseded campaign rule '${id}' is missing superseded_by` when status is superseded and superseded_by is null, and `only a superseded rule may name supersededBy (campaign rule '${id}')` when non-superseded and non-null. Then existingIntervalEnd's own superseded_by null check becomes unreachable — remove it or keep it as an invariant assertion, your call, but say which.

# =============================================================
VERIFIED COHERENT BY THE SUPERVISOR (do not change): strict prospectivity of ordinary create/supersede/revoke (rev10); disputed-turn bounded exception; equal-position supersession (D2); revocation being terminal (a rule revoked at a future position has status revoked immediately, is still active until that position, and can be neither superseded nor re-revoked — intentional, exposed through revokedPosition); later-revoked successor accepted (rev14); rejected mutations atomic; checkpoint restore + typed reads (rev11-13).

# =============================================================
EVIDENCE — a LIFECYCLE MATRIX test, not one test per finding. Add `packages/core/test/campaignRuleLifecycleMatrix.test.ts` (store-backed, real .2 APIs) that, for each of these graphs, (a) builds it through the live mutations where the store allows it, (b) asserts validateCampaignRules(listCampaignRules) accepts it, (c) asserts the active identity set at every boundary position — one before and at each of: each effective position, each revocation position, each successor effective position, plus one far-future ordinal — as literal lists, and (d) round-trips it through serializeCampaign + materializeSnapshot and re-asserts (b) and (c) on the restored DB:
  G1 single active rule; G2 rule revoked later; G3 scheduled rule cancelled (no prior); G4 A->B prospective; G5 A->B then revoke B after effect; G6 A->B->C then revoke C; G7 A scheduled, superseded by B at the same scheduled position; G8 disputed-turn successor at the current turn; G9 disputed-turn successor at the immediately preceding turn across sessions; G10 two rulings for one ambiguity in disjoint intervals (R1 revoked before R2 effective).
And for each REJECTED graph, prove BOTH boundaries reject with their exact messages and that the store leaves rows/active sets unchanged: X1 reverse-time successor (F1, validator) and the store's existing rejection; X2 cancel a scheduled successor before effect (F2, store and validator); X3 two priors -> one successor (F3, validator; store: second supersede naming an existing successor is rejected 'already exists'); X4 overlapping rulings (F4, validator; store rejection message); X5 superseded row without superseded_by / active row with superseded_by (F5, hydration; construct via a test double row or by temporarily dropping the CHECK in a scratch table — say how).
Every negative assertion asserts the distinctive message. NEGATIVE PROOF: run the matrix against 4aaf5e8 before fixing; report exactly which cells fail and with what.

VERIFICATION: npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing; report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local resolution. Do not touch migrations, the position encoding, admission rules other than F2, or context assembly.
notes:
Dispatched 2026-09-05: codex gpt-5.6-luna, effort HIGH, YOLO, worktree .worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev15 (cut from eshyra-jhpt @ 4aaf5e8), pgid 1233131.
Completion report (commit 3a1867b).

Implemented all five lifecycle-graph cells:
- F1: validateCampaignRules now rejects reverse-time successors with successor 'B' cannot take effect before 'A'; equal positions remain valid.
- F2: revokeCampaignRule rejects cancelling a scheduled successor before effect with campaign rule 'B' supersedes 'A' and cannot be revoked before it takes effect; supersede it instead. The validator mirrors this as successor 'B' of 'A' was revoked before taking effect. The module documents cancellation via same-position supersession/copy continuity. Standalone scheduled rules with no prior remain cancellable.
- F3: validator rejects a successor named by multiple priors.
- F4: added the exported internal campaignRuleIntervalsOverlap half-open interval helper; validator and store overlap admission use it, including revoked/superseded endpoints and empty intervals.
- F5: rowToRule now rejects both status/superseded_by asymmetries. The existingIntervalEnd null check remains as an unreachable invariant assertion after fail-closed hydration.

Negative proof against baseline 4aaf5e8: the lifecycle matrix ran with exactly 5 failures (X1-X5) and 10 accepted graphs passing. F1 validator accepted with no message; baseline store emitted successor 'B' cannot take effect before 'A'. F2 store and validator both accepted with no message; the supervisor probe observed active [A] at position 12 and [] at positions 15 and 20, then revoke A emitted campaign rule 'A' is not active and supersede A emitted campaign rule 'A' is already superseded. F3 validator accepted with no message; baseline store emitted campaign rule 'B' already exists. F4 validator accepted with no message; baseline store emitted active ambiguity ruling 'R2' overlaps 'R1' for ambiguity 'amb-matrix'. F5 hydration accepted both superseded-without-successor and active-with-successor rows with no message; the pre-existing domain validator messages were superseded rule must name supersededBy and only a superseded rule may name supersededBy.

Added packages/core/test/campaignRuleLifecycleMatrix.test.ts. G1-G10 build through live store mutations, assert literal active identity sets at every required boundary, validate, and round-trip through serializeCampaign/materializeSnapshot. X1-X5 assert exact store/validator or hydration messages and unchanged rows/active sets. X5 uses a test-double row by temporarily enabling SQLite ignore_check_constraints and direct UPDATE, then restores/asserts no read mutation. No existing test encoded the newly forbidden F2 case, so no test was moved; the existing no-prior cancellation test remains valid.

Verification: npm run verify:worktree passed from this worktree-local resolution: 278 test files passed, 3 skipped; 4921 tests passed, 20 skipped. Focused pre-verification campaign/checkpoint run: 82 passed, 6 skipped.
